reuse.why: The change reuses tag parsing, budget writes, batching, and undo wrappers, but copyPreviousMonth independently implements eligibility instead of sharing the new selection abstraction.

duplication.why: Fixed-group and income exclusions recur across five action loops, while hidden and saved-template eligibility is implemented separately in SQL and copyPreviousMonth.

placement.why: Budget policy stays in server budget actions, tag parsing uses the shared utility, and method registration follows the existing application layer.

scope.why: The edits are confined to the requested month-wide budget actions, their method registration, and related tests.

maintainability.why: The category query reduces existing duplication, but incomplete policy centralization leaves maintainers coordinating eligibility changes across the helper and individual actions.

bypasses_abstraction.where: packages/loot-core/src/server/budget/actions.ts: copyPreviousMonth uses getBudgetData and local eligibility checks rather than sharing getBudgetableCategories or a common eligibility predicate.

disguised_duplication.where: packages/loot-core/src/server/budget/actions.ts: copyPreviousMonth expresses hidden and saved-template exclusions as JavaScript rejection conditions, duplicating the SQL inclusion conditions in getBudgetableCategories.

abstraction_drift.where: packages/loot-core/src/server/budget/actions.ts: getBudgetableCategories gains includeHiddenCategories and its SQL visibility alternative, while copyPreviousMonth retains a separate eligibility implementation and callers retain fixed-group and income exclusions.
